# devhelm_monitor (Resource)

Manages a DevHelm monitor. Supports HTTP, DNS, TCP, ICMP, Heartbeat, and MCP Server probes, and BROWSER and MULTI_STEP_API code monitors. A code monitor points `code.entrypoint` at a Playwright file; the provider uploads the include set at plan time and, on apply, runs a validation run before the code goes live (`test_before_publish`). Next to Terraform, `devhelm test --from-terraform .` runs the configured code without applying it, and `devhelm trigger <monitor>` starts a run of the live code.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# HTTP monitor — the most common case.
resource "devhelm_monitor" "api" {
  name              = "Public API"
  type              = "HTTP"
  frequency_seconds = 60
  regions           = ["us-east", "eu-west"]

  config = jsonencode({
    url             = "https://api.example.com/health"
    method          = "GET"
    timeout_seconds = 10
  })

  assertions {
    type = "status_code"
    # `expected` is a STRING in the API contract — it can hold "200", "2xx",
    # or "200-299". Always quote the value, even for plain numeric codes;
    # `jsonencode({ expected = 200, ... })` (number) plans cleanly but
    # apply fails with "Provider produced inconsistent result" because the
    # API normalizes the value to "200" (string) on the round-trip.
    config = jsonencode({ expected = "200", operator = "equals" })
  }

  assertions {
    type = "response_time"
    # API field names are camelCase inside `config` (the API contract is JSON,
    # not Terraform). Use `thresholdMs`, not `threshold_ms`.
    config = jsonencode({ thresholdMs = 500 })
  }

  alert_channel_ids = [devhelm_alert_channel.ops.id]
  tag_ids           = [devhelm_tag.production.id]
}

# Heartbeat monitor — for cron jobs and batch workers. The job POSTs to
# `ping_url` after each successful run; if no ping arrives within
# `expectedInterval + gracePeriod`, the monitor fires an incident.
resource "devhelm_monitor" "nightly_etl" {
  name = "Nightly ETL"
  type = "HEARTBEAT"

  config = jsonencode({
    expectedInterval = 86400 # 24h
    gracePeriod      = 3600  # 1h slack for slow runs
  })
}

output "etl_ping_url" {
  description = "Hit this URL from your cron job after a successful run."
  value       = devhelm_monitor.nightly_etl.ping_url
}

# Authenticated HTTP monitor with a vault-backed bearer token. The actual
# secret material lives in `devhelm_secret` and is referenced by ID — it
# never enters Terraform state.
resource "devhelm_secret" "api_token" {
  key   = "api_token"
  value = var.api_token # mark as sensitive in your variables.tf
}

resource "devhelm_monitor" "private_api" {
  name              = "Private API"
  type              = "HTTP"
  frequency_seconds = 60

  config = jsonencode({ url = "https://api.example.com/internal/health" })

  # Pick exactly one of: bearer / basic / header / api_key.
  # The API resolves `vault_secret_id` at probe time and attaches the
  # credential — no plaintext ever transits the wire from Terraform.
  auth = {
    bearer = {
      vault_secret_id = devhelm_secret.api_token.id
    }
  }
}

# Custom header (e.g. CF-Access-Client-Secret, X-Auth-Token, …).
resource "devhelm_monitor" "header_protected" {
  name = "Header-protected service"
  type = "HTTP"

  config = jsonencode({ url = "https://internal.example.com/health" })

  auth = {
    header = {
      header_name     = "X-Auth-Token"
      vault_secret_id = devhelm_secret.api_token.id
    }
  }
}

# Basic auth — username:password are stored in the vault entry as a
# colon-separated pair. Provider only references the secret by ID.
resource "devhelm_monitor" "basic_auth" {
  name = "Legacy admin endpoint"
  type = "HTTP"

  config = jsonencode({ url = "https://legacy.example.com/admin/health" })

  auth = {
    basic = {
      vault_secret_id = devhelm_secret.api_token.id
    }
  }
}

# BROWSER code monitor. The provider uploads the include set at plan time
# (`code_hash` is the server's closure digest) and runs a validation run
# before new code goes live.
resource "devhelm_monitor" "checkout" {
  name              = "Checkout"
  type              = "BROWSER"
  environment_id    = devhelm_environment.production.id
  frequency_seconds = 600
  regions           = ["us-east", "eu-west"]
  alert_channel_ids = [devhelm_alert_channel.oncall.id]
  config            = jsonencode({ timeoutSeconds = 90, runtimeId = data.devhelm_runtime.latest.id })

  code = {
    entrypoint = "${path.module}/synthetics/checkout.spec.ts"
    include    = ["${path.module}/synthetics/fixtures/**"] # optional; files that ship without being imported
  }

  capture_policy = {
    screenshots = "on_failure"
    trace       = "on_failure"
    video       = "off"
    network     = "on_failure"
  }
  fast_retry_max_attempts = 1
  run_parallel            = true
  secret_keys             = ["CARD_TOKEN"]
  test_before_publish     = true
  owner_address           = "devhelm_monitor.checkout"
}

# MULTI_STEP_API code monitor: Playwright `request` steps, no browser.
resource "devhelm_monitor" "orders_api" {
  name              = "Orders API flow"
  type              = "MULTI_STEP_API"
  environment_id    = devhelm_environment.production.id
  frequency_seconds = 300
  regions           = ["us-east"]

  code = {
    entrypoint = "${path.module}/synthetics/orders.spec.ts"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable name for this monitor
- `type` (String) Monitor type: HTTP, DNS, TCP, ICMP, HEARTBEAT, MCP_SERVER, BROWSER, or MULTI_STEP_API

### Optional

- `acknowledge_rollback` (String) Rolled-back digest to publish again on purpose; needed when the configured code was rolled back in the dashboard
- `alert_channel_ids` (List of String) Alert channel IDs to notify on incidents. Omit to preserve the current list; explicitly set to `[]` to clear all channels.
- `assertions` (Block List) Monitor assertions that define pass/fail criteria. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--assertions))
- `auth` (Attributes) Monitor authentication. Specify exactly one variant (`bearer`, `basic`, `header`, or `api_key`). Credentials are never sent through the API in plaintext — set `vault_secret_id` to a `devhelm_secret` ID; the probe resolves the secret server-side at check time. The block itself is not marked sensitive because it carries only UUID references; the actual secret material lives on `devhelm_secret.value` which is sensitive. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auth))
- `capture_policy` (Attributes) When to keep screenshots, traces, video and network evidence (code monitors) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--capture_policy))
- `code` (Attributes) Code for a BROWSER or MULTI_STEP_API monitor. The provider uploads the include set (the entry file's directory, or `include`) at plan time; the server resolves the import closure. Forbidden for probes (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--code))
- `config` (String) Monitor configuration as JSON. Shape depends on type (HttpMonitorConfig, DnsMonitorConfig, etc.). Required for probes; optional for BROWSER and MULTI_STEP_API (ScriptMonitorConfig: `timeoutSeconds`, `runtimeId`)
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the monitor is active; omit to leave pause state unmanaged
- `environment_id` (String) Environment the monitor runs in (variables and secret values). Required for BROWSER and MULTI_STEP_API monitors
- `fast_retry_max_attempts` (Number) Fast-retry attempts after a failure; 0 disables
- `frequency_seconds` (Number) Check frequency in seconds (10–86400); the minimum depends on the plan. The server applies the plan minimum when omitted on create. Omit on update to preserve the current value; the API has no way to clear this field.
- `incident_policy` (Attributes) Incident policy controlling when failures escalate to incidents. The API auto-creates a default policy on monitor creation, so omitting this attribute adopts the server defaults; supplying any field overrides the policy in full. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--incident_policy))
- `owner_address` (String) Resource address recorded as the owner declaration, e.g. `module.web.devhelm_monitor.checkout` (Terraform doesn't tell providers the address)
- `owner_enforced` (Boolean) Only Terraform may change this monitor's configuration (default: true on create). Use an API key created with tool TERRAFORM
- `regions` (List of String) Probe regions (e.g. us-east, eu-west). Omit to preserve the server's current regions; explicitly set to `[]` to clear.
- `run_parallel` (Boolean) Run every region each interval; false rotates one region per interval (code monitors)
- `secret_keys` (List of String) Secret keys the code may read; omit to use the keys the server scanned in the code
- `tag_ids` (List of String) Tag IDs to attach to this monitor
- `test_before_publish` (Boolean) Run a validation run before new code goes live (default: true). A failed run stops the apply and the old code stays live. false publishes the code untested in one call
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `code_files` (Map of String) Files in the import closure, each mapped to its content digest; the plan diff lists added, removed and changed files
- `code_hash` (String) Closure digest (sha256:<hex>) the server computed for the configured code at plan time
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for this monitor
- `live_revision_digest` (String) Closure digest of the live revision; differs from code_hash after a rollback
- `live_revision_id` (String) Revision that scheduled runs execute
- `owner` (Attributes) Tool that owns this monitor and what it declared (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--owner))
- `ping_url` (String) Heartbeat ping URL (only set for HEARTBEAT monitors)

<a id="nestedblock--assertions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assertions`

Required:

- `config` (String) Assertion configuration as JSON; the inner `type` field is omitted (set via the sibling `type` attribute) and the rest of the shape depends on the assertion kind. Field names inside the JSON are camelCase (the API wire format) and JSON value types must match the API contract exactly — e.g. `status_code.expected` is a STRING (`jsonencode({expected = "200", operator = "equals"})`, not `expected = 200`), while `response_time.thresholdMs` is a NUMBER (`jsonencode({thresholdMs = 500})`). Type-mismatched values plan cleanly but fail apply with "Provider produced inconsistent result" because the API normalizes them on the round-trip.
- `type` (String) Assertion type discriminator in snake_case wire format (e.g. `status_code`, `response_time`, `body_contains`, `header_value`, `dns_resolves`, `ssl_expiry`, `tcp_connects`). Must match an AssertionType enum value as serialized by the API.

Optional:

- `severity` (String) Assertion severity: fail or warn (default: fail)


<a id="nestedatt--auth"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auth`

Optional:

- `api_key` (Attributes) API key sent in a configurable header. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auth--api_key))
- `basic` (Attributes) HTTP Basic auth. Reference the username/password vault secret via `vault_secret_id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auth--basic))
- `bearer` (Attributes) Bearer token sent in the `Authorization` header. Reference the token via `vault_secret_id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auth--bearer))
- `header` (Attributes) Custom header with an arbitrary name and a secret value resolved from the vault. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auth--header))

<a id="nestedatt--auth--api_key"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auth.api_key`

Required:

- `header_name` (String) HTTP header name that carries the API key (matches `^[A-Za-z0-9\-_]+$`).
- `vault_secret_id` (String) Vault secret ID for the API key value (UUID).


<a id="nestedatt--auth--basic"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auth.basic`

Required:

- `vault_secret_id` (String) Vault secret ID holding Basic auth username and password (UUID).


<a id="nestedatt--auth--bearer"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auth.bearer`

Required:

- `vault_secret_id` (String) Vault secret ID holding the bearer token value (UUID).


<a id="nestedatt--auth--header"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auth.header`

Required:

- `header_name` (String) Custom HTTP header name for the secret value (matches `^[A-Za-z0-9\-_]+$`).
- `vault_secret_id` (String) Vault secret ID for the header value (UUID).



<a id="nestedatt--capture_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `capture_policy`

Optional:

- `network` (String) When network rows and HAR are kept: always, on_failure, or off
- `screenshots` (String) When to capture screenshots: always, on_failure, or off
- `trace` (String) When to capture a Playwright trace: always, on_failure, or off
- `video` (String) When to capture video: always, on_failure, or off


<a id="nestedatt--code"></a>
### Nested Schema for `code`

Required:

- `entrypoint` (String) Path to the file that runs, e.g. `${path.module}/synthetics/checkout.spec.ts`

Optional:

- `include` (List of String) Globs for files that ship even though nothing imports them (fixtures, data), added to the default set: the entry file's directory, recursively, minus node_modules/, dist/, build/, coverage/, *.map, dotfiles and .devhelmignore matches
- `root` (String) Bundle root; paths are uploaded relative to it (default: the nearest ancestor containing .git, else the entry file's directory)


<a id="nestedatt--incident_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `incident_policy`

Optional:

- `confirmation_type` (String) Confirmation strategy type (e.g. multi_region)
- `consecutive_successes` (Number) Consecutive successes required for recovery
- `cooldown_minutes` (Number) Minutes to wait before auto-resolving
- `max_wait_seconds` (Number) Maximum seconds to wait for multi-region confirmation
- `min_regions_failing` (Number) Minimum regions that must fail to confirm an incident
- `min_regions_passing` (Number) Minimum regions passing for recovery
- `trigger_rules` (Attributes List) Rules that determine when failures escalate to incidents. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--incident_policy--trigger_rules))

<a id="nestedatt--incident_policy--trigger_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `incident_policy.trigger_rules`

Required:

- `severity` (String) Incident severity: down or degraded
- `type` (String) Rule type: consecutive_failures, failures_in_window, or response_time

Optional:

- `aggregation_type` (String) Aggregation type: all_exceed, average, p95, max
- `count` (Number) Failure count threshold (1–10)
- `scope` (String) Rule scope: per_region or any_region
- `threshold_ms` (Number) Response time threshold in ms (for response_time)
- `window_minutes` (Number) Time window in minutes (for failures_in_window)



<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--owner"></a>
### Nested Schema for `owner`

Read-Only:

- `address` (String) Resource address the owning tool declares
- `label` (String) Display label the owning tool declares
- `project` (String) Project the owning tool declares
- `type` (String) Owning tool: DASHBOARD, GIT, TERRAFORM, MCP, or API

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Monitors are imported by ID or exact name. The next apply transfers
# ownership to Terraform (shown in the plan as `owner` changing).
terraform import devhelm_monitor.api "Public API"
```
